title: TEMPO: Time Series Understanding via Discrete Tokenization
summary: Time-series interpretation often requires both numerical observations and textual context.
Integrating these inputs into a pretrained language model raises a representation question: how should a signal enter the model's token sequence?
We present TEMPO, which extends an LLM's vocabulary with discrete codes from a context-aware Transformer tokenizer using finite scalar quantization.
key_points: Integrating these inputs into a pretrained language model raises a representation question: how should a signal enter the model's token sequence?
We present TEMPO, which extends an LLM's vocabulary with discrete codes from a context-aware Transformer tokenizer using finite scalar quantization.
operator_view: MALT는 논문 초록을 그대로 복제하지 않고, 철도 PHM과 운영 자동화 관점에서 다시 읽는다.
예약 발행 체계에서는 최신성보다 실제 적용 가능성이 높은 논문을 우선한다.
application_notes: 현장 적용 시 어떤 센서, 운영 루프, 검증 절차와 연결할 수 있는지를 먼저 본다.
기존 블로그의 PHM, Observability, Agentic AI 글과 연결될 수 있는 논문만 발행 후보로 삼는다.
limitations: 초록 기반 초안이라 세부 실험 설정과 한계는 발행 전 보강이 필요하다.
실제 배포 전에는 본문 원문과 도표를 다시 확인하는 절차가 권장된다.
abstract: Time-series interpretation often requires both numerical observations and textual context. Integrating these inputs into a pretrained language model raises a representation question: how should a signal enter the model's token sequence? We present TEMPO, which extends an LLM's vocabulary with discrete codes from a context-aware Transformer tokenizer using finite scalar quantization. A frozen tokenizer maps four-step patches to a 625-code vocabulary; signal tokens, scale statistics, and text are then processed by the LLM's existing self-attention layers. Adaptation updates the new token embeddings and DoRA adapters. With a Qwen3-4B backbone and task-specific fine-tuning, TEMPO achieves macro-F1 scores of 89.0% on activity recognition, 85.0% on sleep staging, and 86.0% on bearing-fault diagnosis. Time-series question answering and qualitative bearing-diagnosis examples further illustrate how this interface combines signal representations with textual context. Together, these results demonstrate the utility of discrete vocabulary extension for time-series understanding.

review.why_selected: 이 논문은 철도 설비, 센서, 고장 진단 같은 블로그 핵심 축과 직접 연결된다. 그래서 단순히 최신 논문이라서가 아니라, 지금 블로그 독자에게 바로 설명할 이유가 있는 후보로 봤다.
review.interpretation: 이 논문은 성능 숫자보다 배치 위치를 봐야 한다. 어떤 센서를 받아 어떤 경보나 유지보수 판단으로 이어지는지 설명할 수 있을 때 비로소 블로그 글로서 의미가 생긴다.
review.applicability: 실무 적용 장면도 비교적 선명하다. 정비 시점 판단, 이상 징후 조기 탐지, 센서 이벤트 해석 같은 흐름으로 바로 이어 설명할 수 있다.
review.caution: 초록만으로는 데이터셋 조건, 운영 제약, 오탐 비용 같은 실전 요소가 충분히 드러나지 않는다. 그래서 발행할 때는 어디까지 믿고 적용할 수 있는지 한계를 같이 말해야 한다.
review.verdict: 내 판단으로는 이 논문은 보관만 할 후보가 아니라, 해석을 붙여 발행할 만한 가치가 있다.

sections.1 introduction: Time-series data record how a system evolves, while text describes the conditions under which those observations should be interpreted. A vibration trace, for example, may have different implications during commissioning and during routine operation. An interpretation therefore often needs to combine temporal patterns with operating conditions, maintenance history, and a user’s question. Task-specific classifiers provide useful predictions, but their output interface is usually a fixed label set. Language models offer a complementary interface: users can ask questions and receive descriptions or explanations. The central challenge is to give a pretrained LLM access to the signal itself. Numerical text serialization, continuous encoder embeddings, and learned discrete tokens make different trade-offs in sequence length, representation, and integration with the language model. TEMPO studies a discrete interface. A separately pretrained tokenizer converts a normalized signal into contextual codes. These codes become additional vocabulary entries, so text and time-series tokens occupy one input sequence and use the same self-attention layers. Per-channel mean and standard deviation accompany the codes as text. This separates waveform shape from scale information while retaining both as model inputs. Our contribution is the combination of a context-aware FSQ tokenizer, direct vocabulary extension, and a two-stage adaptation recipe for time-series tasks. The tokenizer attends over the full observed window before quantization, and the LLM is adapted through new embeddings and DoRA adapters. We evaluate this design on activity recognition, sleep staging, bearing-fault diagnosis, and time-series QA, and analyze the tokenizer encoder representations on UCR datasets.
sections.2 related work: Chronos quantizes scalar values for token-based forecasting ( Ansari et al., 2024 ) ; TimesFM and Moirai develop pretrained forecasting models ( Das et al., 2024 ; Woo et al., 2024 ) . Mantis learns representations for classification ( Feofanov et al., 2026 ) . These systems primarily produce forecasts, predictions, or embeddings. TEMPO focuses on integrating observed signals with natural-language questions and responses. ChatTS, OpenTSLM, TsLLM, and ITFormer connect time-series encoders to language models through continuous representations, including soft prompts or cross-attention ( Xie et al., 2025 ; Langer et al., 2025 ; Parker et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2025 ) . Soft prompts can enter the existing self-attention stream without requiring a separate cross-attention module. Discrete approaches include scalar binning in Chat-TS ( Quinlan et al., 2025 ) and learned vector-quantized representations in TokenCast ( Tao et al., 2025 ) . TempoGPT is a closely related approach that quantizes temporal embeddings and shares an embedding layer between temporal and textual tokens ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) . Shared discrete vocabularies also support multimodal models for vision and audio ( Chameleon Team, 2024 ; Nguyen et al., 2025 ) . TEMPO’s distinguishing design choice is a Transformer encoder with global attention over the input window followed by finite scalar quantization (FSQ) ( Mentzer et al., 2024 ) . Global attention makes the representation of each patch depend on its surrounding signal context, while FSQ maps these representations onto a fixed scalar grid. TEMPO combines this contextual tokenization with direct vocabulary extension and staged LLM adaptation. FactoryBench evaluates LLM reasoning over industrial robotic telemetry through questions about system state, interventions, counterfactuals, and decisions ( Merzouki et al., 2026 ) . In its zero-shot evaluation of six frontier LLMs, no model exceeds 50% on structured levels or 18% on decision-making. These results highlight substantial difficulties in reasoning over industrial time series and motivate interfaces that integrate signal representations with textual context.
sections.3 method: TEMPO comprises a signal tokenizer, an extended LLM vocabulary, and two adaptation stages (Figure 1 ). The tokenizer is trained independently of the language model and remains frozen during LLM adaptation. For channel c c , we compute its mean m c m_{c} and standard deviation s c s_{c} over the observed input window and normalize where ϵ \epsilon prevents division by zero. Each channel is tokenized separately. Its statistics are included in the text context, preserving scale information alongside the normalized shape representation. The tokenizer divides a normalized channel into non-overlapping patches of L = 4 L=4 time steps and projects them to d = 128 d=128 dimensions. A four-layer Transformer encoder applies global self-attention before a projection to four latent dimensions. FSQ quantizes each dimension to one of five levels, giving an implicit vocabulary of 5 4 = 625 5^{4}=625 codes: Here i i indexes patches and P P is the latent projection. A symmetric Transformer decoder reconstructs the normalized signal from quantized representations. The tokenizer is pretrained on approximately 500K windows from nine source groups using reconstruction, multi-scale spectral, and temporal-smoothness losses. Training takes approximately four hours on one A10G GPU. Appendix B gives the training configuration. The encoder can represent a patch differently depending on the surrounding signal. This differs from independent scalar binning and from convolutional encoders whose context is limited by their receptive field. The tokenizer compresses four time steps into each code and uses all 625 codes in the vocabulary-usage analysis. We add 627 entries: 625 signal codes and two delimiters, <ts_start> and <ts_end> . New embeddings are initialized as random vectors scaled to the mean norm of existing embeddings. A gradient mask restricts embedding updates to the new entries. A typical input has the form [user] Signal: (mean=0.12, std=0.45) <ts_start> <ts_207> <ts_14> … <ts_end> What fault is present? [assistant] The numbers and token IDs above illustrate the input format. Signal and text tokens use the existing self-attention blocks. The embedding and vocabulary dimensions are expanded, but the Transformer backbone does not require new attention or gating modules. Only the 627 new embeddings are updated; the tokenizer, backbone, and adapters are frozen. Approximately 200K examples combine discriminative signal tasks (50%), masked-span code prediction (20%), and M4 captions (30%). The discriminative component covers 22 synthetic signal types and 19 task types, with 20% noise augmentation. This stage associates the discrete signal vocabulary with the language model’s existing representation space. We update the new embeddings and DoRA adapters ( Liu et al., 2024 ) , using rank r = 32 r=32 on the attention and MLP projections. The mixture contains approximately 0.26M examples spanning classification, anomaly detection, temporal reasoning, diagnosis, and description. Around 50K text-only instruction examples are included to mitigate language forgetting. Base-model weights and original text embeddings remain frozen. For the in-distribution evaluations, the Stage 1 checkpoint is further fine-tuned on each domain’s training split. Each domain is evaluated with its corresponding adapted checkpoint. The tokenizer remains fixed throughout.
sections.4 experiments: We fine-tune the Stage 1 checkpoint on domain-specific training splits and evaluate on held-out test sets. All TEMPO results in Table 1 use Qwen3-4B. HAR, sleep staging, and bearing diagnosis are evaluated with macro-F1; TSAQA ( Jing et al., 2026 ) classification and anomaly detection use accuracy. † \dagger OpenTSLM macro-F1 values are from Table 2 of Langer et al. (2025) , arXiv v3. GPT-4o HAR/Sleep values are also from OpenTSLM; its remaining scores are from local evaluations. TEMPO reaches 89.0% on HAR, 85.0% on sleep staging, and 86.0% on bearing diagnosis. OpenTSLM with Llama3.2-3B is the closest comparison in model size: SoftPrompt reaches 64.87% on HAR and 54.40% on Sleep; Flamingo reaches 62.77% and 45.45%. TEMPO exceeds both OpenTSLM configurations on these tasks. Specialized models outperform TEMPO on two of the three classification tasks: random forest reaches 96.0% on HAR, and WDCNN reaches 99.2% on bearing diagnosis. Closing this gap remains a challenge for the general-purpose signal-to-language interface. On TSAQA, TEMPO achieves 80.5% classification accuracy and 91.3% anomaly-detection accuracy. The tuned LLaMA3.1-8B baseline reaches 91.3% and 91.0%, respectively. With a 4B backbone, half the size of the 8B baseline, TEMPO achieves comparable anomaly-detection accuracy but trails it on classification. We evaluate transfer to Time-MQA ( Kong et al., 2025 ) using a smaller Qwen3-1.7B TEMPO model with one-shot prompting on 600 questions. Table 2 compares these results with published baselines. † \dagger Baselines reported in Kong et al. (2025) . TEMPO reaches 62% classification accuracy, compared with 52% for Qwen-2.5-7B and 32% for GPT-4o. Its anomaly-detection and judgment scores are lower than both baselines. The lower judgment score is consistent with the capacity gap between TEMPO’s 1.7B backbone and the 7B Qwen baseline. Classification nevertheless remains a strength despite the smaller model size. We analyze code activations on held-out windows from six source groups: ECG, financial, forecasting, synthetic, UCR, and UEA data. The tokenizer uses all 625 codes, with normalized entropy H / H max = 0.889 H/H_{\max}=0.889 . The cosine similarities between domain-level activation vectors are 0.78 for ECG/UCR and 0.73 for financial/forecasting signals. The activation statistics show overlapping code usage across signal families, with particularly similar distributions for ECG/UCR and financial/forecasting signals. We examine a Qwen3-4B checkpoint adapted to bearing-fault diagnosis using 20K examples. The examples use CWRU signals from an SKF 6205-2RS bearing at 1800 RPM. The following examples illustrate how operational context influences the generated responses. For the same vibration trace, the model diagnoses an outer-race fault when told that the bearing is aged. When told that the part is newly installed and non-OEM, it questions whether the observed features reflect a fault or manufacturing variation. The response thus changes with the supplied operating context while the signal remains fixed. Table 3 presents four outer-race fault examples. The recommended action escalates with the ISO zone supplied in the prompt, from monitoring to immediate replacement. In a further example, GPT-4o receives a deliberately incorrect inner-race label together with a numerically serialized signal and produces an explanation consistent with that label. TEMPO instead identifies an outer-race fault in this example.
sections.5 discussion and conclusion: TEMPO integrates observed time series and text through a shared discrete vocabulary and the LLM’s existing self-attention. Its context-aware tokenizer maps four-step patches to a 625-code vocabulary, while textual statistics preserve scale information. This provides a compact signal interface that can be adapted through new embeddings and DoRA adapters while keeping the tokenizer and base LLM weights frozen. With task-specific adaptation, TEMPO achieves 89.0%, 85.0%, and 86.0% macro-F1 on activity recognition, sleep staging, and bearing diagnosis. The QA results extend this interface to natural-language questions, and the bearing examples illustrate responses conditioned on operating context. The linear-probe analysis in Appendix A shows that the tokenizer encoder representations retain information useful for classification. Quantization introduces a trade-off between compression and temporal detail, while separate channel tokenization makes sequence length grow with the number of channels. Future directions include channel-aware compression and adaptation to additional signal domains. FactoryBench ( Merzouki et al., 2026 ) offers a natural extension of the evaluation to industrial questions about interventions, counterfactuals, and decisions. We evaluate the tokenizer encoders by mean-pooling their time-series representations and training logistic-regression classifiers on 15 UCR datasets. The encoders remain frozen during probe training. We compare FSQ-T with absolute positional embeddings, CNN+VQ, and FSQ-T with rotary positional embeddings (FSQ-T-RoPE). All 15 probe datasets occur in the tokenizer pretraining corpus, so the comparison measures representation quality under shared dataset exposure. Sample-level overlap is not documented. FSQ-T has the highest mean probe accuracy, exceeding CNN+VQ by 2.1 percentage points and FSQ-T-RoPE by 3.9 points. Its validation loss is not the lowest, showing that the ordering by validation loss differs from the ordering by probe accuracy. The row-wise maxima give seven wins for FSQ-T, four for CNN+VQ, and four for FSQ-T-RoPE, with no ties at the reported precision. FSQ-T’s largest advantage over CNN+VQ is on GunPoint (+17.4 points); its largest disadvantage is on SmoothSubspace (-16.0 points). The following tables summarize the training settings. The tokenizer is frozen during both LLM adaptation stages. Stage 0 updates 627 new embeddings; Stage 1 additionally updates DoRA adapters. The expanded vocabulary contains 625 signal codes and two boundary tokens. The 200K-example mixture contains 50% discriminative tasks, 20% code imputation, and 30% M4 captions. Discriminative tasks use 22 signal types and 19 question types, with 20% noise augmentation. The mixture lists TSAQA-Benchmark (139K), HAR-CoT (20K), Sleep-CoT (9K), CWRU Bearing-CoT (20K), ECG-QA-CoT (20K), and SlimOrca/Alpaca instructions (50K). The listed components total approximately 0.26M examples. Reported costs are approximately $3 for tokenizer training (four A10G hours), $49 for Stage 0 (five hours on eight H100s), and $34 for Stage 1 (3.5 hours on eight H100s). The total is approximately $86 for the 1.7B pipeline, excluding repeated experiments and downstream specialization. In an exploratory bearing-diagnosis study with Qwen3-4B and 186K training examples, rank 16 produced 9 errors in 30 manually inspected examples. Rank 64 reportedly achieved perfect classification but generated only the bearing template. Rank 32 retained conversational responses with a reported score of 86%.

analysis.one_line: 이 논문은 베어링이나 회전체 신호에서 미세한 이상 징후를 더 안정적으로 분리해, 조기 고장 진단에 쓰려는 접근이다.
analysis.why_now: 이번 글에서 중요한 건 베어링 진단에서 늘 어려웠던 `설비 간 도메인 차이, 정밀 경계 추출, 노이즈와 가림`를 한 번에 다루려 했다는 점이다. 철도 wheelset 쪽 논문은 실험실 데이터에서는 좋아 보여도, 속도와 부하가 달라지면 성능이 크게 흔들리는 경우가 많다.
analysis.problem: 핵심 문제는 정상과 이상 신호가 서로 섞여 있고, 속도 변화나 부하 변화 때문에 같은 고장도 다르게 보인다는 점이다. 그래서 논문은 `신호를 더 잘 펼쳐 보고`, `다른 환경에서도 덜 무너지게` 만드는 방향을 택한다.
analysis.method_overview: 본문에서 눈에 띄는 구성은 TEMPO, Time Series Understanding, Discrete Tokenization TEMPO, LLM 쪽이다. 쉽게 말하면 신호를 시간축 그대로 보지 않고 주파수나 시간-주파수 표현으로 다시 펼친 뒤, 장비가 바뀌어도 특징이 덜 무너지도록 학습시키는 흐름이다.
method_steps: 먼저 문제를 현장 단위로 다시 정의한다. 즉, 단순 분류가 아니라 실제 점검이나 유지보수 판단에 필요한 출력 형태를 만든다.
그다음 모델 쪽에서는 TEMPO, Time Series Understanding, Discrete Tokenization TEMPO 같은 요소를 묶어 성능과 배치 가능성의 균형을 맞춘다.
마지막으로 결과를 바로 숫자 자랑으로 끝내지 않고, 잡음·환경 변화·실시간 처리 같은 운영 조건에서 버티는지 확인하려 한다.
analysis.experiment_read: 실험은 한 장비나 한 속도 조건에서 배운 모델이 다른 조건으로 넘어갔을 때도 버티는지를 보는 데 초점이 있다. 그래서 최고 정확도 숫자 하나보다 `다른 조건에서도 유지되는가`를 먼저 읽는 편이 실무에 더 가깝다.
experiment_points: 논문이 제시한 비교는 단일 정확도보다, 기존 방식 대비 어디서 덜 무너지는지를 보는 게 중요하다.
본문과 초록에서 바로 읽히는 수치 신호는 정확도, 처리 속도, 모델 크기 쪽이다.
실무적으로는 최고 점수보다도 데이터 조건이 달라져도 결과가 유지되는지, 그리고 경보 이후 작업 흐름에 연결되는지가 더 중요하다.
analysis.interpretation: 내가 이 논문을 발행 가치가 있다고 보는 이유는, `좋은 모델 하나`보다 `운영에 붙일 수 있는 구조`를 보여주기 때문이다. 블로그 관점에서는 이 논문을 읽고 나면 어떤 센서나 이미지가 들어오고, 어떤 판단 출력으로 이어져야 하는지 머릿속에 그릴 수 있어야 한다.
analysis.field_reality: 베어링 진단 논문은 실험실에서는 좋아 보여도 실제 운영에 붙이면 신호 품질, 회전 속도 변동, 장비 차이, 라벨 부족 때문에 성능이 빠르게 흔들릴 수 있습니다. 그래서 이 글은 모델 이름보다도 어떤 조건에서 성능이 유지되는지, 그리고 경보가 정비 의사결정으로 자연스럽게 이어질 수 있는지를 중심으로 읽는 편이 좋습니다.
evaluation_questions: 실험 데이터의 속도·부하 조건이 실제 노선이나 설비 조건과 얼마나 비슷한가
학습한 특징이 다른 장비나 다른 계절 조건으로 넘어가도 유지되는가
경보 결과를 사람이 재검수하거나 정비 우선순위로 연결할 절차가 있는가
limitations: 본문이 제시하는 실험 조건이 다른 노선, 다른 장비, 다른 계절에도 그대로 유지되는지는 추가 검증이 필요하다.
실제 유지보수에서는 오탐 비용과 미탐 위험을 함께 봐야 하므로, 논문 성능 수치만으로 바로 운영 정책을 정하긴 어렵다.
현장 배포 단계에서는 모델 자체보다 데이터 수집, 라벨 품질, 검수 프로세스가 병목이 될 가능성이 크다.
analysis.closing: 쉽게 말해 이 논문은 `이론적으로 좋아 보이는 방법`을 넘어서, 현장에 붙일 때 무엇을 더 챙겨야 하는지 생각하게 만드는 타입이다. 그래서 하루치 자동 발행 글이어도, 단순 초록 번역보다 운영 해석을 중심으로 읽는 편이 맞다.
reader_fit: 철도/회전체 설비의 상태 감시 체계를 설계하는 PHM 엔지니어
진동·주파수·시간-주파수 특징을 실제 고장 진단 파이프라인에 붙여야 하는 데이터 분석가
실험실 성능이 아니라 속도 변화, 부하 변화, 장비 차이까지 보고 싶은 운영 담당자
operational_takeaways: 센서 배치, 샘플링 주기, 회전 속도 정보가 우리 설비에서 얼마나 안정적으로 확보되는지 먼저 확인한다.
특히 운영 제약 조건에서 성능이 유지되는지 별도 검증용 데이터셋을 따로 잡아두는 편이 좋다.
파일럿 단계에서는 조기 경보의 민감도보다 오탐 이후 작업 부담이 얼마나 생기는지도 같이 측정한다.
논문 수치만 보지 말고, 우리 데이터 조건과 입력 품질이 논문 조건과 얼마나 다른지 먼저 비교한다.
모델 도입 전에 경보 이후의 사람 작업 흐름까지 같이 설계해야 실제 운영 가치가 생긴다.
